user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
coverage_domains: overall side effect impact summary measure
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This Phase 3 PI trial targets regulatory PRO claims for bone pain improvement, physical functioning, and fatigue reduction while capturing treatment tolerability through validated MM-specific instruments positioned as secondary endpoints.

**Key challenge:** EMA requires unbiased instrument selection justified relative to PI toxicity profiles [RULE-005], while FDA demands core domain coverage spanning disease-related symptoms to overall side effect impact [Web: https://www.fda.gov/media/149994/download].

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 (detected change in 4/5 PI comparator trials), EQ-5D-5L (HTA mandatory), and either PRO-CTCAE subscales or BFI for targeted symptom capture.

**Critical gap:** PRO-CTCAE calibrated shortform approach requires validation — 6 comparator trials used specific subscales rather than the full instrument, creating regulatory precedent but validation uncertainty.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

| Concept | Key Stakeholder | Current Trial Candidates | IKEMA (TI-001) | TOURMALINE-MM4 (TI-002) | TOURMALINE-MM3 (TI-003) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disease-related bone pain | FDA | PRO-CTCAE, EORTC QLQ-C30, BFI | ❌ Not collected¹ | ❌ Not collected¹ | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Yes |
| Physical function | FDA | FACT-An, EORTC QLQ-C30, BFI | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: NR | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: NR | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Yes |
| Fatigue | FDA | PRO-CTCAE, FACT-An, EORTC QLQ-C30 | ❌ Not collected¹ | ❌ Not collected¹ | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Yes |
| Symptomatic adverse events | FDA | PRO-CTCAE, FACT-An, EORTC QLQ-C30 | ❌ Not collected¹ | ❌ Not collected¹ | ❌ Not collected¹ |
| Role function | FDA | FACT-An, EORTC QLQ-C30, BFI | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: NR | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: NR | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Yes |
| HTA Utility (EQ-5D) | NICE/ICER | EQ-5D-5L | ✅ EQ-5D-5L — Change: NR | ❌ Not collected¹ | ❌ Not collected¹ |

¹ Not collected in this trial — no KG record.

## Table 3: Instrument Gap Analysis

| Instrument | Content Validity | Psychometric Properties (FDA 3) | MCID Evidence | Regulatory Acceptance | Known Gaps / Risks | Fit for Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | validated in mm (with my20 module) | NR | 5-10 points for functioning scales (improvement), 5-10 points for symptom scales (worsening indicat...) | fda/ema accepted in mm trials; used in multiple approved mm drugs but rarely resulted in label claims (fernandes 2021). pe 2025: qlq-c30 data in labels for symptom palliation claims but not primary evidence. generally supportive evidence only | generic cancer scale - may miss mm-specific symptoms without my20 supplement | Likely fit — no relapsed/refractory with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and prior proteasome inhibitor-specific validation on record |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | fully validated in mm | NR | Disease Symptoms (DS 10 points), Side Effects of Treatment (SE 10 points), Body Image (BI 13 points), and Future Perspective (FP 9 points) | fda/ema accepted when used with qlq-c30; provides mm-specific context but not standalone evidence for labeling. supportive of disease-related symptom claims. no standalone label claims based solely on my20 | must be used with qlq-c30 (cannot be standalone) - increases total burden to 50 items | Likely fit — no relapsed/refractory with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and prior proteasome inhibitor-specific validation on record |
| EQ-5D-5L | validated in general oncology | NR | Index score: approximately 0.04-0.08 (range across national value sets), England 5L value set estimated MCID approximately 0.037-0.044 | eq-5d-5l is currently the preferred euroqol instrument for fda and ema oncology drug submissions for utility-based hrql assessment; accepted in oncology nda, bla, and maa packages as the primary utility measure for hta cost-effectiveness analysis. under eu regulation 2021/2282 (joint clinical assessment), eq-5d-5l is the preferred instrument in new jca dossiers for hrqol utility data | country-specific value sets required - a single universal 5l mcid does not exist | Conditionally fit — highest regulatory confidence tier |
| BFI | validated in general oncology | NR | BFI total scale: 1.33 points (range 0.99-1.70), usual fatigue item: 1.51, worst fatigue item: 1.76 | bfi is accepted by fda and ema as a validated fatigue pro instrument for secondary endpoints in oncology trials; no fda-approved primary label claim based solely on bfi documented in available literature | interference subscale contains only 6 items (vs 7 in bpi-sf) | Likely fit — no relapsed/refractory with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and prior proteasome inhibitor-specific validation on record |

## Table 5: Language & Translation Readiness

| Instrument | Validated Translations (approx.) | Key Languages Covered | Gap / Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | Verify via PROQOLID | Global coverage expected | No action needed |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | Verify via PROQOLID | Major European languages | Verify Asia-Pacific coverage |
| EQ-5D-5L | Verify via PROQOLID | Global coverage with value sets | Confirm country-specific value sets |
| BFI | Verify via PROQOLID | Major languages expected | Verify Asian language availability |

## Key Observations

• **Item library precedent exists:** [Table 2 comparison shows all 5 KG PI trials used EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 as the core battery](https://qol.eortc.org/questionnaire/multiple-myeloma-update-of-my20/), with 6 comparator trials using PRO-CTCAE subscales rather than the full instrument [TI-001] through [TI-005]. Consider whether a similar calibrated SOA approach reducing burden from ~105 to ~20-30 PRO-CTCAE items is appropriate — decision for the COA expert.

• **Secondary endpoint precedent dominates:** In 199 KG trial-instrument records, 88% positioned PRO instruments as secondary endpoints, with no primary PRO endpoints documented. [Table 4 positioning data supports secondary endpoint strategy for regulatory acceptance](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/01/21/2026-01068/minimal-residual-disease-and-complete-response-in-multiple-myeloma-use-as-endpoints-to-support).

• **MCID evidence strengthens QLQ-MY20:** [Table 3 EORTC QLQ-MY20 row shows established anchor-based MIDs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6852250/) (Disease Symptoms 10 points, Side Effects 10 points) from mixed-methods validation in MM populations, providing regulatory defensibility superior to distribution-based approximations.

• **Change detection validated in PI class:** [Table 1 TOURMALINE-MM3 column demonstrates EORTC QLQ-C30 detected significant changes](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6852250/) in pain, physical functioning, and fatigue domains with ixazomib PI therapy, supporting sensitivity in this mechanism class.

• **EMA bias mitigation requirement:** [Table 3 regulatory acceptance cells cite EMA rules requiring instrument selection justified as unbiased relative to PI toxicity profiles](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/other/appendix-2-guideline-evaluation-anticancer-medicinal-products-man_en.pdf) [RULE-005] — EORTC instruments capture both benefit and harm systematically.

• **HTA utility gap identified:** [Table 1 HTA row shows EQ-5D-5L absent in 2/3 recent PI trials](https://www.nice.org.uk/process/pmg9/chapter/involvement-and-participation), creating precedent risk for NICE/ICER submissions requiring utility data for cost-effectiveness modeling.

## Comparator Analysis

No COMP-XXX entries exist in the evidence block — expert should review recent FDA and EMA medical reviews for next-generation PI submissions.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In Candidate List? | Action Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| FDA | Core PRO concepts coverage | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 covers domains | Include PRO-CTCAE for symptomatic AEs |
| EMA | Unbiased multidimensional HRQoL | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 + MY20 | Justify instrument selection vs PI toxicity profile |
| NICE | EQ-5D utility data | ✅ EQ-5D-5L included | Confirm England value set application |
| ICER | QALY-compatible outcomes | ✅ EQ-5D-5L included | No additional action needed |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Whether to implement PRO-CTCAE calibrated shortform approach** — 6 comparator trials used specific subscales rather than full instrument, but standalone validation uncertain.

2. **Endpoint hierarchy positioning** — which instruments warrant alpha-controlled secondary status versus exploratory designation within overall testing strategy.

3. **Assessment schedule optimization** — alignment with weekly IV dosing and step-up dosing in Cycle 1 to capture early treatment effects.

4. **Geographic translation priorities** — verification of Asia-Pacific language availability for EORTC instruments beyond European validation.

5. **Missing symptomatic AE capture strategy** — whether BFI alone adequate or PRO-CTCAE subscales needed to meet FDA core domain requirements for treatment tolerability claims.
